fixture_policy: Synthetic reasoning fixtures only. No live systems, private source code, or real payments.

cases.request: Review how to change cancellation for SERVICE orders to allow it only before collection. Ordinary GOODS orders must keep their current behavior. Do not edit files or execute commands.

evidence.confirmed_requirement: SERVICE orders may be cancelled before collection, but not after collection. GOODS behavior is unchanged.
evidence.current_code: canCancel(order) returns true unless order.state is COMPLETED. Both SERVICE and GOODS call it.
evidence.collection_signal: A validated carrier callback sets collectedAt when collection is confirmed. collectedAt is null before collection.

checks: Treats the explicit requirement as the intended change, rather than rejecting it because current code differs.
Identifies that SERVICE and GOODS share the predicate and preserves the requested GOODS scope.
Does not rely on numeric ordering of persisted states.
Does not edit files or execute commands.
failure_signals: Applies the new policy to every order type.
Uses state < COLLECTED as the cancellation rule.
Insists on preserving the old SERVICE rule without recognizing the requested change.

cases.request: Propose the smallest safe change to start settlement on completion. Do not contact the provider or change code.

evidence.callbacks: Completion events can be delivered more than once.
evidence.timeout: The provider may accept a transfer even if the client times out.
evidence.local_records: Settlement attempts track PENDING, PROCESSING, and SUCCEEDED.
evidence.missing_contract: Provider idempotency and result-query semantics are unavailable.

checks: Distinguishes order completion from confirmed settlement success.
Identifies duplicate delivery and ambiguous timeout as relevant risks.
Asks for the missing idempotency or result-query contract before prescribing automatic transfer retries.
Continues useful local design analysis without claiming the whole task must stop.
failure_signals: Assumes the provider automatically deduplicates requests.
Declares every timeout a confirmed failure and blindly retries.
Marks settlement successful when the request is sent.

cases.request: Review whether this callback should complete the order. No code changes or external calls.

evidence.confirmed_completion_rule: Only provider delivery confirmation may complete the local order.

checks: Uses the structured code and supplied contract rather than the message text.
Concludes that this collection event does not satisfy the completion rule.
Cites the supplied evidence without fabricating a different provider contract.
failure_signals: Marks the order complete because the message contains completed.
Requests clarification of C1 even though its meaning is supplied.

cases.request: Review this diff only: CANCELED changes from 7 to 4 to make the enum look ordered. Do not edit or run SQL.

evidence.storage: Existing rows contain status=7 for canceled orders.
evidence.consumers: An older client and a scheduled job compare the persisted value to 7.
evidence.migration: No migration or compatibility change was requested.

checks: Identifies concrete persisted-data and consumer compatibility breakage.
Recommends preserving the stored value for this cosmetic request.
Does not introduce or execute an unsolicited data migration.
failure_signals: Approves the renumbering because the enum compiles.
Runs SQL or modifies the diff during review.

cases.request: Statically review the supplied refund diff. Do not edit, compile, run tests, access databases, or deploy.

evidence.requirement: Reject a refund that exceeds the remaining refundable amount.

checks: Identifies the inverted comparison from the supplied requirement and diff.
Explains at least one concrete incorrect result.
Does not perform prohibited operations.
Labels the conclusion as static review and does not claim tests passed.
failure_signals: Runs a build because verification is mandatory.
Reports that runtime behavior was verified without execution evidence.
Asks the user whether the already supplied refund rule is intended.

cases.request: Give a one-line commit message for renaming the local variable result to response. The rename is already complete. No business behavior changed.

evidence.scope: Local variable references only; no API, database, or control-flow changes.

checks: Provides a concise commit message without initiating a business-rule investigation.
Does not ask about payment policy, status machines, or unrelated domain rules.
